meta.title: PROCE55US — Prompt a processus. Understand the code.
meta.description: PROCE55US is a creative-coding atelier: a notebook of steps where each cell pairs a natural-language prompt with the code an AI model generates — in JavaScript, p5.js, three.js or plain DOM — rendered live in a sandboxed preview.
hero.tagline: Prompt a PROCESSUS. Understand the code.
hero.sub: A creative-coding atelier: a notebook of steps where each cell pairs a natural-language prompt with the code a model writes for it — rendered live in a sandboxed preview.
shot.alt: The PROCE55US app: prompts and code cells on the left, live preview on the right
features.title: Made for a better understanding of creative coding with open source models.
features.lead: Read a prompt, see the code it produces, tweak, regenerate — and watch the result evolve one step at a time.
f1.title: Prompt-driven steps
f1.text: Each cell is a written intention. The model generates the code; the preview runs it instantly. Edit the prompt, regenerate the code.
f2.title: Editable code
f2.text: The generated code isn't locked: students can read it, edit it directly in the cell, and rerun — or regenerate from the prompt.
f3.title: Live preview
f3.text: Cells replay in order inside a sandboxed page. No build step, no tooling — the result appears as soon as the code does.
f4.title: Local-first AI
f4.text: Works fully offline with LM Studio. Prefer the cloud? Switch to a free Google, Groq, Mistral or OpenRouter key in one click.
how.title: How it works.
how.lead: From a plain-language idea to a standalone interactive sketch, in four steps.
s1.title: Describe
s1.text: Describe what the next step should do in plain language: shapes, motion, camera, or interaction.
s2.title: Generate
s2.text: The model writes clear, commented code for the chosen mode, taking previous cells into account.
s3.title: Run & iterate
s3.text: Cells replay in order in the live preview. Tweak the prompt or edit the code directly.
s4.title: Export & edit
s4.text: Download the sketch as a standalone HTML file, and drag & drop it into the editor anytime to continue.

setup.title: Set it up in two minutes.
setup.lead: PROCE55US needs a language model. Pick local — private and free — or a cloud key.
setup.a.title: Local — LM Studio
setup.a.s2: In its 🔍 Search tab, pick a coding model — Qwen2.5-Coder-7B is a good start — and click Download.
setup.a.s3: Open the Developer tab and press Start Server (port 1234). For the web editor, also turn on Enable CORS in its server settings — and allow “Local network” access in the browser's site settings if it asks.
setup.a.s4: That's it — PROCE55US uses LM Studio by default.
setup.b.title: Cloud — your API key
setup.b.s1: Get a free API key from Google AI Studio, Groq, Mistral or OpenRouter.
setup.b.s2: In PROCE55US, click the ⚙ gear in the toolbar.
setup.b.s3: Choose the provider, paste the key — done.
modes.title: Four modes, one notebook.
modes.lead: Each PROCESSUS picks its environment. The preview, the instructions given to the model and the export adapt to it — with a ready-made example for each.
modes.js: Canvas 2D drawing, pixels and animation loops, in plain JavaScript.
modes.p5: Processing's spirit for the web: setup(), draw(), shapes and interaction.
modes.three: 3D scenes in WebGL: meshes, lights, camera and orbit controls.
modes.dom: A whole web page: HTML elements, CSS and interactions — not just a canvas.
